label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
Kiran,

Thanks for this. I’ve just finished a run of nights, so forgive me if this is more direct than polished — but I wanted to answer properly rather than leave it sitting.

Appa, Amma — I’m not writing any of this to make a point to you. I just want Kiran’s questions answered in the open.

First, before the logistics: I am genuinely thrilled that Amma and Appa are coming. That hasn’t changed, and I don’t want it to get lost under the rest of this.

You’re right that you should have been asked earlier. I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and that was exactly the point I should have looped you in. I didn’t, and that’s on me. It wasn’t meant to be a decision taken behind your back. The idea actually came from Appa, not me — in August, on the phone, Rohan was showing him the vegetable patch and he said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” I ran with it after that.

On Appa’s heart — you’re right that visitors don’t get free NHS treatment, and we’re not relying on that. This is the UK long-term visitor visa, max six months per visit, and the plan is first week of April to end of September 2027. I’ve got them a travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, about £640 each for the six months, and the agent says it covers the stent. Dr Prakash has agreed to do Appa’s review in March before they fly, and a video consult in July. He’s happy to share his notes with me, and I can pass anything relevant on to you. The annexe at the back is finished — ground floor, no steps, its own shower with a grab rail. Leicester Royal is 15 minutes from our house and I know half the cardiology team. That doesn’t make it the same as being at home, but it’s not nothing.

On Amma and six weeks — that’s fair, and I don’t want to pretend it isn’t. The thing that makes it feel workable is that she isn’t stuck here: the return ticket is flexible and she can go home any time. She’ll also have her own space in the annexe rather than being a guest in the spare room.

On Ganesh Chaturthi — it isn’t gone. Two options as I see it: they could fly Leicester to Pune for it in September and finish the trip there, or the Pune lot could come here in August. I’m happy to cover the Pune family’s flights for an August visit. Whichever Amma and Appa prefer.

I don’t read your email as trying to spoil anything. These are the questions I’d ask in your position, and I’d rather we talked them through properly than did it by email. Can we do a family video call this Sunday, 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? I’ll send the link.

Anika has made a laminated welcome timetable. It includes “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays.” So you can see the children have already decided.

Love,
Meera
